subject.title: MEDIA: tokens inside markdown code fences are silently ignored

question: Should final-reply `MEDIA:` tokens inside fenced code blocks stay non-delivered with a warning, or should standalone valid fenced tokens be extracted as attachments?
rationale: Current source intentionally preserves fenced examples as text, but the reported problem is silent attachment loss; extraction changes transcript semantics, while warn-only leaves delivery behavior unchanged and makes the failure diagnosable.

options.title: Land warn-only diagnostics
options.body: Review and land the linked delivery-boundary warning shape so fenced tokens remain text but emit one clear warning when delivery was likely intended.

options.title: Extract fenced standalone tokens
options.body: Change the parser contract to deliver valid standalone fenced `MEDIA:` tokens, accepting the risk that example snippets may become attachments.

options.title: Document as by design
options.body: Keep runtime behavior unchanged and rely on docs/template guidance, leaving runtime delivery silent unless a separate diagnostic is added.

recommendation.title: Land warn-only diagnostics
recommendation.body: Review and land the linked delivery-boundary warning shape so fenced tokens remain text but emit one clear warning when delivery was likely intended.

likelyOwner.reason: They provided the live review direction on the linked fix and are tied to the current parser/reply path in main history.
